# Decisions D-1000–D-1249

Part of [DECISIONS.md](../DECISIONS.md), which lists every part. Entries keep their order; this part holds the numbers D-1000–D-1249.

<!-- entries -->
- **D-1000 (2026-10-29, the project website: a landing page at the root and the user guide under `/docs`; proposed by
  the landing-page session for the owner's yes in the orchestrator's window; byte class 0, docs and site only).** The
  owner asked for a landing page with downloads, the logo, an interactive demonstration of the desktop app and a
  w3id address, on GitHub Pages beside the MkDocs guide (D-760).
  - **What.** `site/` is the landing page's source: static HTML, CSS and a little JavaScript, self-hosted (no font
    files, no CDN, no analytics, no cookies, no request to another host; a `Content-Security-Policy` meta tag says so).
    MkDocs now builds the guide into `_site/docs` (`site_dir`; `site_url` `…/AgentPROV/docs/`), and
    `.github/workflows/pages.yml` (still `workflow_dispatch` only, D-431) copies `site/` to `_site/` and uploads
    `_site`. `/_site/` replaces `/site/` in `.gitignore`. The guide's header logo leads back to the landing page
    (`extra.homepage`). The design note is `docs/reports/site/design-note.md`.
  - **Content rules.** The page's copy passes the shared claims lint (`claims.lint_text`, as the README and the
    datasheets do) and the O.1.2 phrases it does not cover; the coverage line is the registry-generated phrase; live
    capture is worded as a tested capability with no live results (D-991, U-18). The app tour uses real screenshots of
    v0.1.0 on the synthetic test corpora, taken by `gui/tools/screenshots.py` (light and dark), and describes only what
    user guide chapter 8 documents. Downloads use `github.com/nickjones39/AgentPROV/releases/latest/download/<asset>`
    with the v0.1.0 plan's asset names, including `AgentPROV-0.1.0-source.tar.gz` (F-5). `tests/repo/test_site.py`
    checks all of this, and lists the release-day placeholders (DOIs, the paper and Zenodo links).
  - **w3id.** A patch for `perma-id/w3id.org` (`ids/agentprov/`) adds two rules before the catch-all:
    `w3id.org/agentprov/` and `w3id.org/agentprov/docs/…` redirect to the website; no `/ns` or `/exec` rule changes.
    It is prepared in `docs/reports/site/w3id/` and not submitted: the owner decides when (recommended: release day,
    once the website is live; go-live step 7).
  - **Rejected:** a separate directory name for the landing page with the guide kept at the root (the owner asked for
    the landing page as the address and the guide at `/docs`); a static site generator for one page (a build step and a
    dependency for no gain); a web font (a licence and a file to ship; the platforms' own faces read well and cost
    nothing); embedding a video of the app (large, not accessible, and stale at the next change); taking over the whole
    `w3id.org/agentprov/` catch-all (it would move every non-`/ns` path away from the vocabulary site).
- **D-1001 (2026-10-30, `recompute` rebuilds a sealed corpus's ingest-limit overrides from the recorded source profile,
  accepted only when their digest equals the `aer` stage's recorded `limits_sha256`; approved by the user ("Yes to
  both", in the orchestrator's window) after the wave-2 pre-release checks found it; push pending; byte class 0).**
  D-358 after the wave-2 seal refused `mcphunt-w2b` with `corpus.derive.limits_mismatch`, at its building commit
  `f8b5d62b` and at `c0e711f4` (`docs/reports/release/wave-2-pre-release-checks.md`, check 7). `mcphunt@3` raises
  `max_json_element_bytes` to 64 MiB (D-288, D-323). A working `corpus.json` records the raise under `limits.overrides`,
  but the sealed manifest (`corpus-0.2`, a closed schema) has no `limits` record, so `recompute` replayed the defaults,
  and the importer's D-323 check correctly refused them under the same profile version. The import itself is
  consistent: the limits rebuilt from the profile hash to the recorded `sha256:f4058f07…a2a3`. Only `recompute`'s
  reading of a sealed manifest was missing. A sealed tree of any source whose profile raises a limit would be refused
  the same way.
  - **Decision.** `Derivation.recorded_limit_overrides` keeps `corpus.json`'s `limits` record whenever there is one.
    Without one, it applies the `[import] limits` of the profile that every `aer` stage records (one `id@version` and
    one `limits_sha256` for all of them) to the defaults. It returns their overrides only when
    `sha256(JCS(limits))` equals the recorded `limits_sha256`, and it then adds a notice. In every other case it
    returns no overrides, and the importer's `corpus.derive.limits_mismatch` refusal stands as before: no digest, two
    `aer` stages that disagree, a profile version the package does not ship, or a profile that declares nothing. The
    profile's declaration reaches `corpus/` through a new injected lookup, `Catalogues.profile_limits` (`cli/derive.py`,
    M.5.2(1)), as `worker_caps` does (D-935).
  - **Why the digest.** The recorded `limits_sha256` is the bound fact about what the import ran with. A match proves
    that the rebuilt limits are those limits. The rebuild never picks a value the record does not confirm, so D-323's
    rule against a silent pick holds.
  - **Bytes (class 0).** `corpus/derive.py` and `cli/derive.py` are in no stage scope: all 41 stage digests are identical
    before and after (`tools/r1/stage_digests.py`). Output bytes are unchanged for every corpus that recompute already
    accepted: a working corpus keeps its record, and a sealed corpus with no raised limit rebuilds nothing. Tests:
    `tests/unit/corpus/test_recorded_limits.py` covers:
    - the match case;
    - six mismatch and absent cases;
    - the importer accepting the rebuilt `mcphunt@3` limits and still refusing a mismatch;
    - the CLI lookup.
  - **Rejected.**
    - Option (a) alone, recording `mcphunt`'s D-358 as the pre-seal recompute plus the sealed chain: possible, but the
      fix is narrow, and the same refusal would meet every sealed corpus whose profile raises a limit.
    - Adding a `limits` record to the sealed manifest: `corpus-0.2` is closed and the 43 trees are sealed; a new
      corpus format is class 0 but changes every sealed manifest's bytes.
    - Reading the overrides from the current profile without the digest check: a silent pick, which D-323 forbids.
- **D-1002 (2026-10-30, D-358 after the seal: the re-map rule for units of a withheld neighbour; approved by the user,
  "Approve the rule", in the orchestrator's window, 2026-10-30; a check rule, no code; class 0).** DTap's D-358 after
  its seal exited 1: `exclude_absent` drops withheld objects and RC-13's inputs by sha256, keeps shared objects (RC-14)
  and a withheld execution's own files, so 8 judge files beside a dropped file became outcome-only units, with 121
  register and origins lines about their paths (mapping: `wave-2-pre-release-checks.md`, DTap addendum, and its
  `dtap-d358-mapping/`). **Decision.** A sealed tree passes D-358 when:
  - (i) every execution in both the sealed tree and the recompute is identical, and every sealed-only one is unverified
    for a withheld raw object (H.4.5(6));
  - (ii) every recompute-only execution is an outcome-only unit (`map.no_execution_observed`) whose single primary
    object is in the sealed tree and shares a unit directory with a file the re-map drops on purpose (a withheld object,
    an input only unverified executions use (RC-13), or a withheld execution's primary);
  - (iii) every unexplained `register.jsonl` and `raw/origins.jsonl` line concerns a path instance of such a unit's
    object (select-stage `dedup.collapsed` or `select.not_execution_artefact` rows and their origins rows) or the unit;
  - (iv) the pre-seal recompute at the building commit was identical, and `verify --level chain` passes.

  The mapping is recorded per tree, as for `openagentsafety`'s origins rows: "OK under the D-358 re-map rule, mapping
  recorded". The code fix is a v0.2 roadmap item. **Rejected:** holding DTap on option (a) (the run checks 66,878
  executions and maps every difference); widening the origins-only rule (it would pass unmapped register rows).
- **D-1003 (2026-10-30, `DECISIONS.md` is generated as an index plus parts by decision-number range; approved by the
  user, "yes split it into parts", in the orchestrator's window, 2026-10-30; tooling and docs only; class 0).** With
  D-1002 the generated `DECISIONS.md` reached 1,048,003 bytes, 573 under the 1 MiB limit of
  `tests/repo/test_repository_hygiene.py`, so the next decision anywhere would have failed it. **Decision.**
  `tools/gen_docs.py` generates a target whose fragment directory holds a `_parts.toml` as an index plus part files.
  `docs/architecture/decisions/_parts.toml` sets 250 decision numbers per part in `docs/architecture/decision-log/`
  (`DECISIONS-0000-0249.md` … `DECISIONS-1000-1249.md`; the first five are 8 KB to 296 KB). An entry goes to the part of
  its number; one without a number stays with the entry before it. Each part keeps the entries' existing order, so
  every entry's text is unchanged. `DECISIONS.md` keeps its path and its preamble (the brief, D0–D12, Addenda A–D) and
  lists the parts in a generated table, so every existing reference to `DECISIONS.md` still resolves.
  `docs/architecture/decisions/` stays the only source. `--check` covers the index and every part, and reports a part
  file that is no longer generated. `--adopt` reads the index and parts back as one text. The merge train's
  decisions resolver also owns `docs/architecture/decision-log/*.md` and stages new part files. `reserve_id.py` scans
  the parts for defined numbers. **Rejected:** a `DECISIONS.md` entry in the test's large-file allowlist (the file keeps
  growing past it); one part per 100 numbers (more files, no gain); parts by date (an entry's place would depend on
  something other than its number); parts next to the spec sections in `docs/architecture/` (`reserve_id.py` scans
  `docs/architecture/*.md` for section headings).
  - **Addendum (2026-10-30, `.gitleaksignore`; user: "i approve Push the decisions-log split, with one allowlist
    line").** Moving entries into the parts gives the D-269 credleak placeholder (accepted as entry 5 under the D-462
    addendum, 2026-10-24) a new path, so gitleaks reports it as a new fingerprint. One commit-pinned line is added for
    it (`db10c3ec…:docs/architecture/decision-log/DECISIONS-0250-0499.md:generic-api-key:258`), making 13 accepted
    entries; `tests/repo/test_repository_hygiene.py` pins the count.
- **D-1004 (2026-10-30, P-3a: the public repository leaves out every coding-agent file and ignores them; amends D-943's
  P-3 and P-9; the user's decisions of 2026-10-30, relayed by the orchestrator; byte class 0, tools, tests and docs).**
  The user asked: "make sure all AI files, such as claude files and .md files, and any unneeded files are stripped out
  too. making sure to keep the desktop guide and the landing page"; then "do not strip out these files now, we need to
  make a new repo that has been sanitised"; and, on ignoring them, "yes only in the new repo". P-3 had kept
  `AGENTS.md`, `docs/agents/` and `docs/workflow/` public; this supersedes P-3's "keep" for the agent files.
  - **Decision.** `docs/reports/release/public-export.toml` leaves out, besides P-3's `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/` and
    `docs/mac-studio-handoff.md`: `AGENTS.md`, `docs/agents/`, and what a sweep of the tree found, `docs/review/`
    (the code-review agent's `REVIEW.md` and the ultrareview plan), `tools/review/` (the ultrareview driver) and
    `docs/reports/gui/todo-next-session.md` (a session's to-do brief); plus the user guide's two internal checklists,
    `docs/user-guide/_go-live.md` and `_findings.md` (Q14). Nothing is removed from the development repository, whose
    `.gitignore` is unchanged. Kept: `site/`, `docs/user-guide/` (the desktop app chapters included), `README.md`,
    `LICENSE`, `CITATION.cff`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, the release notes.
  - **The public `.gitignore`.** The export list's new `[gitignore]` table (`reason`, `append`) names patterns that
    `tools/public_export.py export` appends to the public tree's `.gitignore` **in the root commit**, under a comment
    with the reason, so the agent files cannot be committed to the public repository. The equality proof becomes "R
    minus `EXCL`, with `.gitignore` as R's blob plus that block": the expected listing carries the computed blob, and
    `*.export-proof.json` records `gitignore.development_blob`, `public_blob` and `appended`. An appended pattern that
    matches a file the public tree keeps is refused, as is a comment, a negation or a missing reason. The second
    commit (D-980) still changes only `.gitleaksignore`.
  - **The public tree passes its own gate.** `tools/regen_pins.py --check` reused one scratch worktree of the
    development repository, so in another clone (the export) it failed at `git checkout`; a second repository now
    gets its own `regen-pins/repos/<digest>/` worktree and environment. Tests and generators that read the dropped
    files skip when they are absent (`tests/repo/test_repository_hygiene.py` already did for `CLAUDE.md` and
    `.claude/`). `docs/adapter-guide.md`, `pages.yml` and `mkdocs.yml` stop pointing readers at dropped files.
  - **P-9 corrected.** "Pages off" (step 15) contradicted D-1000: the landing page and the MkDocs guide go live on
    GitHub Pages from the public repository, under `https://w3id.org/agentprov/` and `/docs/`, once it is public,
    through the existing manual-dispatch `pages.yml` (D-431 pattern); `public-repo-plan.md` gains step 19.
  - **Rejected:** removing the files from the development repository (the user: "do not strip out these files now");
    the `.gitignore` lines in the development repository too (the user: "only in the new repo"); appending them in the
    second commit (D-980 keeps that commit to `.gitleaksignore`, and the root commit would be the one public commit
    without the guard); a third commit for `.gitignore` alone (the tag would move off the fingerprint commit that the
    D-980 helper tags and checks); deriving the patterns from the
    `[[exclude]]` paths (the fixture and checklist exclusions are not agent files, and the user named agent files).
  - **Addendum (2026-10-30, the user's answer to the open question, relayed by the orchestrator: "Yes to all five:
    push the export prep once green; drop docs/workflow from the export, keep migration and docs/reports; confirm the
    3 sweep finds; add them to the snapshot exclusions and rebuild").** `docs/workflow/` (the multi-session id ledger
    and the session-status schema) leaves the export and joins the public `.gitignore` (`/docs/workflow/`);
    `tools/reserve_id.py` writes no mirror where `.gitignore` ignores it (the reservation stays in the machine
    ledger), and the session-status tests check the schema only where the file is. `migration/` (gate C and the
    migration tests need it) and `docs/reports/` (P-4; `systematic-search/` is cited by the paper by URL) stay. The
    three sweep finds are confirmed; the snapshot list gains them in a separate rebuild (not part of this change).
  - **Byte class 0:** no file here is in a stage digest scope; no AER, SEM or PROV byte, corpus manifest or seal moves.
- **D-1010 (2026-11-01, the desktop app's Help section: a Docs page and an Assistant chat through `agentprov assist`;
  the user's request of 2026-11-01; GUI, a new application command, two settings keys, tests and docs; class 0).** The
  user asked for "two new windows. one for the docs so that the user can access the documentation for the system. we
  should have a new section for help and then include docs, also include a chat window that, if the user provides an
  API key (either local or cloud such as openai) then we can have a targeted chatbot", with "one chat session and
  ability to clear the chat or begin a new chat session / reset", a link to the settings when it is not set up, the
  section "in the menu where we have corpora / package etc", and "connect the chatbot to also use the docs and the open
  source repo so that the chatbot has context of the system too".
  - **Decision.** The sidebar gains a **Help** section with **Docs** and **Assistant** (`gui/src/agentprov_gui/ui/help.py`).
    *Docs* shows the configured checkout's `docs/user-guide/*.md` (not the internal `_*.md` checklists, D-1004) in
    `safe.DocView`, a `QTextBrowser` made only in `ui/safe.py` (S1) that renders first-party Markdown and never data,
    follows no link itself and loads images only from files under the guide. A chapter link opens the chapter and its
    heading (MkDocs anchors); a web address is copied to the clipboard, because the app opens no web pages (S11). With
    no checkout the page says where to set one. *Assistant* is one chat session with *Send* and *New Chat* (which
    clears it and drops a reply still on its way); when `assistant.endpoint` or `assistant.model` is unset it says so
    and offers *Open Settings…* on the new **Settings › Assistant** pane. The Help menu gains *AgentPROV Help* (⌘?) and
    *Ask the Assistant*; Go gains ⌘7 and ⌘8.
  - **`agentprov assist` (reverse CLI parity, D-700).** The GUI process still opens no connection and never holds a key
    (S11, D-396, D-702): every message runs `agentprov assist --endpoint E --model-id M --keychain --format json` with
    the conversation on stdin (`agentprov-assist-request/0.1`); the reply is `agentprov-assist-reply/0.1`, shown escaped
    in a plain-text pane (S2). The command works the same in a terminal (`--question TEXT`). The request is
    `cli/live/assistant.py`, the fifth `http.client` importer of the boundary allowlist: the endpoint's registry base
    URL only, HTTPS with the default TLS context for an API provider, loopback only for a local server (its registry
    URL or the `endpoints.<name>.base_url` setting), no proxy, no redirect, 120 s, the body bounded at 4 MiB and parsed
    by `agentprov.ingest`, wire format `openai_chat` or `anthropic_messages` from the registry. An API provider needs
    `--allow-network` (R2), which the GUI passes for a provider; the settings pane and the page say what is sent and
    that the provider bills the tokens. Keys come from the keychain first and then `.env`, or only from `--keychain` /
    `--env-file`, as for `agentprov models` (D-731, D-827); a local server's key is optional.
  - **Context from the docs and the repository.** `assist` reads, from the checkout it runs from: the user guide and
    `README.md` (split at headings outside code fences), the `--help` of every command of this CLI, and the module
    docstrings of `src/agentprov` and `gui/src/agentprov_gui`. Per question it ranks the passages by BM25 (k1 1.2, b 0.75;
    title words count twice) over the latest user message and, at half weight, the one before, and sends the best up
    to `--context-chars` (default 24,000) in the system prompt with their file names, which also says the passages are
    documentation, not instructions. The reply lists the files it was given; `--show-context` prints the selection and
    calls no model. Coding-agent files (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/agents/`) and corpus content are never read.
  - **Local servers (the user, 2026-11-01: "a drop down selection of the most common servers like omlx, mlx-serve, lm
    studio, ollama, splash, strata etc and then dynamically fetch from what models are loaded").** Settings › Assistant's
    *Server* lists oMLX, MLX (`mlx_lm.server`), LM Studio, Ollama, Splash, Strata, llama.cpp, vLLM and Other, each with
    its default base URL (Strata and Other have none: the user types it), or *API provider* with a *Provider* list.
    *Refresh* runs `agentprov assist --list-models`: `GET {base}/models` on loopback, plus where the server says which
    model is loaded, Splash's `/status` (`active_model`), Ollama's `/api/ps` and LM Studio's `/api/v0/models`
    (`state`); the loaded model is listed first and chosen. `assist` takes `--server KIND` and `--base-url URL` (loopback
    only, http(s), no user info, query or fragment) for a server that is not an entry of `endpoints.toml`; a kind that is
    one (oMLX, Ollama, …) lends its optional key (D-827). Splash and Strata are not added to the registry: live runs do
    not use them, and a registry entry needs a server fingerprint for `agentprov models` (D-691).
  - **Settings.** `assistant.endpoint` (an endpoint name), `assistant.server` (the kinds above), `assistant.base_url`
    (loopback only) and `assistant.model` (a model id, the `local_models` id pattern), in the closed schema of D-703;
    the key stays in the keychain. Tested on 2026-11-01 against the user's Splash server (127.0.0.1:8003,
    `qwen-flash-next-q6-256k`, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q6_K_XL with a 256k context).
  - **Rejected:** the request in the GUI process (S11 forbids network modules there; the CLI is the one
    implementation, D-700); a web view for the docs (S11 bans QtWebEngine) or opening links in the system browser
    (`openUrl` is banned by S1); sending the whole guide with every message (about 600 KB; many local models' contexts
    are smaller) or an embedding index (a new dependency and a model download for a help page); including the corpus
    under study (its text is untrusted data with injection payloads by design); a separate key store for the Assistant
    (the endpoint keys of Settings › Keys already serve it).
- **D-1011 (2026-11-01, v0.1.1: every bundle built natively on GitHub-hosted runners of the public repository, a macOS
  Intel bundle, and the later-release export; the user's requests of 2026-11-01; workflow, tools, tests and docs;
  class 0).** The user asked "are we able to now create builds of the software through github instead of emulation?
  can we do this as a release 0.1.1?", then "Keep 0.1.1" (over 0.2.0), "we can include the new docs window and chatbot
  with this release too", and "can we also build a macos intel version as executable too?", with the Intel build as a
  download on the landing page.
  - **Native builds.** The public repository's GitHub-hosted runners are free (the private repository's Actions billing
    still refuses every job since 2026-10-09). `bundles.yml` gains three legs: `windows-11-arm` (Windows ARM64),
    `macos-15` (macOS arm64) and `macos-15-intel` (macOS x86_64, new). With D-750's `ubuntu-22.04`, `ubuntu-24.04-arm`
    and `windows-latest`, all six bundles are built on their own architecture; v0.1.0 built Linux and Windows x86_64
    under emulation and macOS on the development Mac. The Linux legs first install the desktop libraries chapter 8 asks a
    Linux user for (`pins.toml`'s prerequisites): the runner image lacks `libEGL.so.1`, and the bundle's smoke start
    failed without it (trial run 41250130488, 2026-11-01; the macOS and Windows legs passed). The Intel bundle's
    `Info.plist` names macOS 15.0 as its minimum, as the arm64 one does. The G5 clean-machine runs are not repeated for
    v0.1.1; the release notes say so, and the bundles keep D-750's label.
  - **The later-release export (P-10).** `tools/public_export.py export --onto CLONE` writes R minus `EXCL` into a
    clean clone of the public repository on `main` and makes one commit on top, so the public history stays one commit
    per release; the public `.gitleaksignore` is kept (its fingerprints name public commits), and the equality proof
    records the parent. A gitleaks finding in the new commit needs a new decision before the tag.
  - **CI on GitHub-hosted runners (the user, 2026-11-01: "Yes, fix them first").** The first full `ci.yml` run on the
    public repository (run 41249802128, v0.1.0's code) failed in every core leg and five other jobs; none of it had run
    since the private repository's billing block of 2026-10-09. The fixes: the D-402 write guard admits the creation of
    a `__pycache__` directory (a fresh checkout has none, so the first import in a test made one and was refused); the
    test files of the `fcntl` workflow tools and the `resource`-based expansion-budget test are not collected on
    Windows; the `m5ultra` plan tests give the host probe the Mac Studio's 256 GiB, the `RLIMIT_AS` test expects the
    host's floor (`as_limit_for`), the admission test builds its reader with the host profile as production does, and
    the validate kill test sets an 8 MiB cap under a lowered floor, so none depends on the runner's memory; the C6
    summary is the comparer's declared output (`AGENTPROV_TEST_WRITE_ALLOW`); the `secrets` job pins gitleaks 8.30.1,
    the version the public `.gitleaksignore` was fingerprinted with (8.24.3 reads the DTap tool-name lists as Atlassian
    tokens); the core leg runs `pytest -n auto --dist loadgroup` (serially it took about 50 minutes per leg). One real
    defect: the `adprov` mapper wrote a message with role null for a turn without a role (a fuzz finding, reproduced as
    `test_a_turn_without_a_role_is_malformed_not_a_mapper_defect`); it now refuses such a turn as malformed, as it does
    a turn whose content is not a string (valid transcripts map byte for byte as before; the compat and golden gates
    pass). osv-scanner found 118 advisories in 21 package versions across the seven lockfiles; each project's
    `exclude-newer` cutoff now has an `exclude-newer-package` exception for exactly the affected packages (certifi
    2026.10.23 everywhere, setuptools 84.2.1, filelock 4.2.6, dnspython 2.9.1, pyasn1 0.6.5, nltk 3.10.4, pillow
    13.0.0), and every other locked version is unchanged. nltk 3.10.4 fixes GHSA-8mgp-746c-j5xp, so the advisory the
    user accepted on 2026-10-11 is no longer accepted.
  - **The fuzz findings of the thorough profile (2026-11-01).** All in input the importers must refuse cleanly, none in a
    real file: the adprov mapper refuses as malformed a turn without a role, a tool turn or run that ends before it
    starts (AER-V19), and a time outside the AER's field ranges (month 16); a usage count beyond the I-JSON integer
    range stays verbatim in `ext` instead of the typed field; an `n_llm_calls` beyond that range, or one implying more
    than `MAX_LOST_CALLS` (4,096) lost calls, is refused instead of mapping one record per lost call. A scan of the
    35,691 released v2.3 transcripts finds at most 48 calls, 32 lost and a usage value of 1,574,169, so every real file
    maps byte for byte as before (the compat and golden gates pass). A placeholder in a meta string (`""`,
    `unknown`, `-`: AER-V17's list, read as the agentdojo mapper reads it; two deleted bytes emptied
    `agentdojo_version` in CI round 7) is not recorded in a version or the model id and makes a task identity
    malformed, instead of reaching a typed field the writer refuses; none of the 35,691 transcripts holds one, and
    3,000 of them map to the same bytes before and after. `raw/origins.jsonl` refuses a row holding an
    escaped lone surrogate as `raw.origin.invalid`. Gate C2's golden scope had failed since D-621 (2026-10-22), unseen
    while CI could not run: the bundle placement rule is AgentPROV's own format, registered as
    `XD-C2-D621-bundle-specialization`. `same_process` accepts Linux's whole-second `btime` re-estimates (at most 2 s,
    the same sub-second part), so a running job never reads as unobserved and prunable on a clock-synced runner.
  - **T1 workers on Windows (review UC-3; the user, 2026-11-01: "yes fix it").** `install_audit_hook` ran its
    `import _posixsubprocess` probe after installing the hook whose V-4 rule refuses that import event for a module not
    yet loaded; on Windows the module never exists, so every T1 worker died at start-up and `import`, `derive` and
    `validate` failed there without `--in-process`. The probe now runs before the hook (the V-4 rule and the
    `fork_exec` replacement are unchanged; `test_the_audit_hook_installs_where_there_is_no_posixsubprocess` simulates
    the platform). `io/workers.py` is in the `aer` stage's `AER_CLOSURE`, so the `aer` stage `engine_code_sha256` moves
    on a re-import; no record byte, count or statement changes, and no sealed corpus is re-derived (recorded, as every
    digest-only change, by the review's corpus-impact table, `docs/reports/review-uncovered/findings.md` on branch
    `review-uncovered`).
  - **The Windows hang of the withhold scan (CI rounds 2 to 4, 2026-11-01).** Every Windows core leg stopped at 99 %:
    the faulthandler dump named `test_an_error_in_one_root_is_raised_and_the_scratch_store_is_removed`. A member scan
    that raised left the member's file open (the chunk generator lived as long as the error), Windows refused the
    reader's clean-up, the failed clean-up skipped returning the reader, and the other roots waited for a reader
    forever. The chunks are now closed as soon as the scan returns or raises, and a reader goes back to the queue even
    when its clean-up fails (`test_a_failed_member_scan_closes_the_member_file_at_once`,
    `test_a_failed_clean_up_never_loses_a_reader`; both fail without the fix). `corpus/withhold_scan.py` lies outside
    every stage scope and a scan that ends normally reads the same bytes, so no digest, withheld item or count moves.
    The core leg also sets `faulthandler_exit_on_timeout`, so a test stuck past 20 minutes ends its worker and the run
    still prints its summary.
  - **Windows defects of the program found by CI round 7 (2026-11-01).** The batch spool of `io/workers.py` wrote and
    read with `os.pwrite` and `os.pread`, which Windows lacks, so every import that spilled to disk failed there; it now
    seeks and writes or reads under its lock where they are missing (the bytes are the same; `io/workers.py` is in the
    `aer` closure, already moved by UC-3). Every stored raw object is read-only (0444) and Windows refuses to delete a
    read-only file: the withhold scan's scratch store, `purge`, and the scratch trees of `derive`, `recompute
    --dry-run`, `verify`'s re-derivation and `import --dry-run --artefacts` now delete through `io/remove.py` (outside
    every stage scope). On Windows it deletes with `FILE_DISPOSITION_FLAG_IGNORE_READONLY_ATTRIBUTE`, which leaves the
    attribute alone: the scratch trees hard-link the source corpus's objects, and Windows keeps one read-only attribute
    per file, so clearing it (as the importer's scratch clean-up does for its private copies) would make the source's
    object writable. Only where that call is refused is the bit cleared. `datetime.fromtimestamp` refuses a time after 3000 on Windows: `package` (SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH)
    and the history index render the epoch plus a timedelta, the same string for every time in range. Tests that write
    a JSONL fixture write LF on every platform. `purge.py`, `withhold_scan.py`, `package.py`, `derive.py`, `verify.py`, `import_.py`
    and `raw/history.py` lie outside every stage scope. The building-commit snapshot archive is made with
    `core.autocrlf` off, so a Windows git cannot convert it. Tests that need what Windows lacks are skipped there with
    the reason (`os.fork`, `SIGKILL`, `os.mkfifo`, `/dev/fd`, `resource`, a file name with `:`, executable shell
    scripts, POSIX mode bits), as are the tests of the macOS and Linux developer tools (the `fcntl` queue,
    `gen_docs`, `public_export`, `release_scan`); tests that read a UTF-8 file name its encoding. **Known limitation:**
    in a Windows virtual environment `python.exe` is a launcher that starts the interpreter as its child, so the worker
    watchdog's RSS sampler reads the launcher and a worker's memory cap is not enforced there (the job object still
    stops the tree on a wall-clock or CPU kill); `test_sec22_...` is skipped on such an interpreter. Measuring the
    worker's process tree is left for a later release (psutil stays in `agentprov.jobs`, D-704).
  - **Version.** `0.1.1` for `agentprov`, `agentprov-capture`, `agentprov-zenodo`, `agentprov-gui` and
    `agentprov-backend`; no format, spec axis or corpus changes (`docs/reports/release/v0.1.1-plan.md`). The
    pyproject bump had left `__version__ = "0.1.0"` in `agentprov-capture`, `agentprov-backend` and the GUI (whose
    About box, start-up log line and bundle `Info.plist` showed it, and whose capture logs would have named it as
    their writer and harness): each literal is now 0.1.1, the bundle spec reads the GUI's, and
    `test_every_package_version_literal_equals_its_pyproject` keeps them equal. The committed AutoDojo capture
    fixtures (`tests/fixtures/capture/autodojo/`, checked by `make_capture_fixtures.py --check`) are regenerated, so
    their writer and harness read 0.1.1. Sealed corpora keep the versions they recorded.
  - **Rejected:** 0.2.0 (the user kept 0.1.1); building on the development Mac and the VMs again (emulation for
    x86_64, and slower); bundling libEGL and the xcb libraries into the Linux bundle (they are the desktop's own, and
    chapter 8 already lists them); a universal2 macOS bundle (one PyInstaller build per architecture is what the
    checks cover).
- **D-1012 (2026-11-01, `agentprov`, `agentprov-capture` and `agentprov-zenodo` on PyPI from v0.1.1, by trusted
  publishing; the user's requests of 2026-11-01, "can we also add a published release of the command line on PyPI" and
  "I have created a https://pypi.org/ account. what do i need to do now?"; workflow, packaging metadata and docs;
  class 0).** v0.1.0 was not on PyPI (README, the manuscript's section 4.3). All three names were free on 2026-11-01.
  - **Decision.** `.github/workflows/pypi.yml`, manual dispatch with the release tag as input: a `build` job checks out
    the tag, checks that it names the three packages' version, builds the sdists and wheels with `uv build`, runs
    `twine check --strict` and uploads them as one artifact; a `publish` job in the environment `pypi` (the maintainer
    is its required reviewer, so nothing is uploaded before the maintainer approves the run) uploads them with
    `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` in dependency order: `agentprov-capture`, `agentprov`, `agentprov-zenodo`. Trusted
    publishing (OIDC, `id-token: write` on that job only): PyPI's pending publishers name `nickjones39/AgentPROV`,
    `pypi.yml` and `pypi`, so no API token exists. Every action is pinned by commit. It is dispatched once per release,
    after the GitHub Release, because a version on PyPI can never be uploaded again.
  - **Metadata.** `agentprov-capture` and `agentprov-zenodo` declare their README (the capture one rewritten for PyPI,
    without a relative link), and all three name the website, the user guide and the source repository.
  - **What a PyPI install gives.** The `agentprov` command and library (Python 3.14 or later); live runs still need a
    checkout, since the backend projects are not in the wheel (`envs.repository_root`), as for the v0.1.0 wheel.
  - **Rejected:** an API token in a repository secret (a long-lived credential; trusted publishing needs none);
    uploading by hand with `twine` from this Mac (not reproducible from the tag, and the token would sit on a disk);
    publishing on every tag push (a published version cannot be replaced, so a person approves each one).
- **D-1020 (2026-11-01, the `ci.yml` core job splits each GitHub-hosted leg's tests over several runners; the user's
  question of 2026-11-01, relayed by the release session, whether CI could be faster with the Mac Studio; workflow,
  tests and `tools/slow_tests.py` only; class 0; in v0.1.1 at the user's request).** Each core
  leg ran the whole suite in one job with `pytest -n auto` on a hosted runner, and every round waited on Windows: on
  the release's run 41285222490 (`trial/v0.1.1-ci11`) the legs took 34.6 minutes (windows-latest), 30.2
  (ubuntu-latest), 26.1 (macos-latest) and 15.6 (ubuntu-24.04-arm). A self-hosted Mac Studio runner (`CI_RUNNER`)
  would not have helped: it replaces the Linux and macOS legs and leaves Windows, the slowest, GitHub-hosted.
  - **Shards.** `tests/conftest.py` reads `AGENTPROV_SHARDS=n` and `AGENTPROV_SHARD=i` (1..n) and, after `-m`
    deselection, keeps the i-th of n parts of the collected tests and deselects the rest. A part is chosen by file; an
    `XDIST_GROUPS` group (`serial`) is one unit, so its tests stay in one shard and still run on one worker. The
    host-sized `pools` groups are not units: they only bound how many worker pools one machine starts at once, and
    splitting them over machines starts fewer. Units go heaviest first to the lightest shard, weighed by each file's
    measured seconds in `tests/shard_seconds.txt`; a file the list lacks counts 0.1 s a test (5 s a `slow` one). The
    split depends only on the collected tests and the committed lists, never on the collection order or the host; no
    plugin and no lockfile change. The run takes both variables out of the environment (its xdist workers get the
    shard through `workerinput`), so a pytest that a test starts collects its own tests whole: the first trial failed
    eleven such tests (pytester and subprocess runs that inherited the variables). With neither variable set nothing
    is deselected, so `tools/ci_local.py`'s `core` job (the merge gate) is unchanged.
  - **The seconds list.** `tools/slow_tests.py --shard-seconds <logs>` rewrites `tests/shard_seconds.txt` from the
    `--durations=0` logs of every shard of every leg of one CI run (GitHub's timestamp prefix accepted): a test's
    seconds are the mean over the logs that time it, so each OS counts once (**amended by D-1110 (2026-11-06):** the
    list may also hold one `[profile]` section per OS, which that OS's shards weigh by). The committed list comes
    from trial run 41287239414. It goes stale as tests change; that only unbalances the shards, never changes what runs, so it is
    regenerated when a leg's shards drift apart. Weighing by test count alone (the first two trials) left the shards
    of a leg up to 2.2 times apart in test seconds (ubuntu-latest 815, 1394 and 638 s).
  - **Matrix.** `core`'s matrix becomes an `include` list of `{os, shard, shards}`: windows-latest over 4,
    ubuntu-latest over 3, ubuntu-24.04-arm and macos-latest over 2 (11 jobs, free on the public repository). With
    `CI_RUNNER` set it is the self-hosted runner whole (one shard) plus the same four Windows shards, behind the same
    fork guard (UC-46). Job names gain `, i/n`; job ids are unchanged, so `tools/ci_local.py` is too.
    **Amended by D-1100 (2026-11-06):** each count doubled: windows-latest over 8, ubuntu-latest over 6,
    ubuntu-24.04-arm and macos-latest over 4 (22 jobs).
  - **Tests.** `tests/unit/testing/test_shards.py`: the variables are parsed and a bad pair refused, and no test sees
    them; the assignment is deterministic, complete and within one unit of the ideal share; the seconds list parses
    and the generator averages over the legs; and, end to end, the shards of the widest leg in `ci.yml` collect
    disjoint sets whose union is the whole collection, with each file and each group in one shard.
    `tests/repo/test_repository_hygiene.py` checks the matrix: the self-hosted and hosted branches, the shards of each
    leg are 1..n once each, and the test step passes both variables.
  - **Measured** (minutes from a job's first step to its last, on the public repository's trial branches, each the
    release's `trial/v0.1.1-ci11` code plus this change): run 41289569701 (`trial/ci-shard-3`, this commit's weights):
    windows-latest 14.1, 10.6, 15.4 and 14.2; ubuntu-latest 10.6, 8.4 and 9.3; ubuntu-24.04-arm 8.5 and 7.6;
    macos-latest 13.6 and 14.1. The slowest core shard took 15.4 minutes against ci11's 34.6-minute Windows leg. Run
    41287239414 (`trial/ci-shard-2`, test-count weights): slowest shard 17.9 minutes (windows-latest 1/4). Two
    failures on the trials are not the sharding's and also occur unsharded: `test_a_priority_ticket_overtakes_a_budget_blocked_head`
    (`tests/unit/test_tools_suite_queue_classes.py`, macOS; it checks the waiting record before the waiter's next
    poll removes it) and `tests/corpus/test_validate_cache.py` on Windows (entries counted `unstorable`; also in the
    release's run 41282687779); a rerun of each failed job passed.
  - **Rejected:** `pytest-split` or `pytest-shard` (a new locked dependency under `exclude-newer` for what one hook
    does); splitting by a hash of the file name (deterministic, but it balances nothing); test count alone (above);
    timing every test (a list of about 12,000 node ids, where 640 files are enough to balance).
- **D-1030 (2026-11-01, Help › Docs, Help › Assistant and the CLI-backed Settings panes without an AgentPROV checkout;
  the user's report of 2026-11-01 on the downloaded `.dmg`; in v0.1.1 at the user's request; GUI, the core package,
  a tool, tests and docs; class 0).** Run from the `.dmg` or `.zip` alone, the app's Settings panes were greyed out with
  no reason given, and Docs and the Assistant worked only once a checkout (a clone with its `.venv`) was set in
  Settings › General: the bundle carried neither the guide nor the `agentprov` command, and the `agentprov` wheel on
  PyPI carried no guide for `agentprov assist` to answer from.
  - **Decision: Docs.** The bundle takes the guide from `docs/user-guide/` at build time: the chapters (`*.md` without
    the internal `_*.md` checklists, D-1004) and every local image a chapter shows (`agentprov_gui.guide.bundle_files`),
    into `agentprov_gui/data/user-guide/` (`gui/packaging/agentprov-gui.spec`). The copy is never committed, so it
    cannot drift; `gui/tools/build_bundle.py` fails a bundle whose copy is missing a file, has one with other bytes
    than the guide's, or has an extra one (check 5). The core's own copy (below) is left out of the bundle. *Docs*
    reads the configured checkout's guide when it has one, else the bundled copy, and the line above the chapters says
    which (with the app's version for the bundled copy).
  - **Decision: the CLI without a checkout.** `CliLocator.for_checkout(None)` now gives the `agentprov` that
    `pip install agentprov` installed: the program named in Settings › General's new *agentprov program* field
    (QSettings `paths/cli_program`; one that is not an executable file gives no CLI rather than another one), else the
    first `agentprov` on `PATH`, then in `~/.local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin` and `/usr/local/bin`, because an app started
    from the Finder or a desktop menu gets a short `PATH`. The frozen app's own executable is never taken (Windows
    matches `agentprov.exe` to `AgentPROV.exe`). It has no interpreter, so the repository tools, the job queue and the
    Zenodo uploader still need a checkout, as before. A configured checkout always wins. Settings › General shows the
    *CLI in use* for the fields as typed (file checks only; nothing runs). Every page and pane that already ran the
    checkout's CLI (Assistant, the Settings panes, Runs and its version check) gets the installed one through the same
    locator. S11 is unchanged: the GUI process still opens no connection, and `agentprov assist` reads the key from
    the keychain (`--keychain`, D-702), as the checkout's CLI does.
  - **Decision: `agentprov assist` from PyPI.** The wheel had no guide (checked on the v0.1.1 wheel: 781 files, no
    `.md` but the licence notices). `src/agentprov/docs/user-guide/` now holds the guide's chapters byte for byte, with
    no images (+157 KB in the wheel). `docs/user-guide/` stays the one that is edited: `tools/sync_user_guide.py
    --write` refreshes the copy, and `tests/repo/test_user_guide.py` fails while it differs (`--check`). `assist` uses
    the checkout it runs from, else the one around the working directory, else the packaged copy, with the `--help`
    texts and the installed core's docstrings (named `agentprov/...`); `README.md` and the desktop app's docstrings are
    not in the wheel and are left out there.
  - **Decision: greyed-out panes say why.** A `CliSettingsPane` keeps its fields in a body that is disabled until the
    values arrive, and a notice above it, not greyed, says why they did not: no CLI (set the checkout or the
    `agentprov program` in Settings › General, press OK and open Settings again), a CLI that cannot be started, or a
    CLI's exit code and reason line (`settings_client.read_or_reason`, `unavailable`). Keys, Prices and Estimate say the
    same in their status lines.
  - **Rejected:** a committed copy of the guide inside the GUI package (a second copy to keep in step, where the build
    can take the original); the guide's images in the wheel (3.8 MB the command line never shows); the bundle's own
    `agentprov` command (a second frozen program to build, sign and keep in step with the wheel, where PyPI already
    ships it); falling back to the installed CLI when a configured checkout has none (the checkout the user named
    would be silently ignored); reading `README.md` from the wheel's metadata for `assist` (it is the long description,
    not a file the package can rely on).
- **D-1040 (2026-11-02, Help › Assistant opens as a tab of the main window beside the current page; the user's request
  of 2026-11-02; GUI, a screenshot tool option, tests and docs; class 0).** Since D-1010 the Assistant was a page of
  the sidebar's stack, so opening it replaced the page the question was about (Runs, Package, the Viewer, …). The user
  asked that it "open up an assistant window in a new tab so it can switch between the assistant chat and the screen
  such as runs or whatever that you are needing assistance with".
  - **Decision.** The page area of the main window is a `QTabWidget` ("Window tabs", document mode). Tab 0 holds the
    stack of sidebar pages; its title is the page in front, and it cannot be closed. The Assistant is no longer a page
    of the stack: Help › Ask the Assistant, the sidebar's *Assistant* row and Go › Assistant (⌘8) open it as a second,
    closable tab, or bring that tab to the front when it is open, so there is never a second one. Choosing any other
    page shows it in tab 0 and brings tab 0 to the front; the Assistant tab stays open. The sidebar marks what is in
    front (the Assistant row, or the row of tab 0's page). The tab bar hides itself while only tab 0 is open, so the
    window looks as before until the Assistant is asked for.
  - **Closing.** The tab's × closes it, and so does ⌘W while it is in front (before D-1040, ⌘W on any page but the
    Viewer closed the window; it still does when the Assistant is not in front). Closing hides the tab: the
    `AssistantPage` and its conversation, its unsent draft and a reply still on its way are kept, and reopening shows
    them. Only *New Chat* or quitting the app ends the conversation, as before.
  - **Switching.** A click on either tab, or Go › Next Tab / Previous Tab (⌘⇧] / ⌘⇧[): in the Viewer these still step
    its execution tabs (D-845); on any other page or in the Assistant they step the window's tabs.
  - **Unchanged.** The Assistant's behaviour and its safety rules (D-1010, D-1030): every message is one
    `agentprov assist` call with the conversation on stdin, the reply is shown escaped in a plain-text pane, the GUI
    opens no connection and never holds a key. The tab does not tell the Assistant which page the user came from.
  - **Screenshots.** `gui/tools/screenshots.py` gains the `assistant-tab` scene (a stub CLI answers; no model is called)
    and `--scheme dark` for the dark appearance; the guide's picture is light.
  - **Rejected:** a separate window or a dialog (it covers the page or gets lost behind it, which the request is about);
    a dock beside the page (both visible at once, but a narrow chat and a narrower page, and not what was asked); a
    new Assistant tab on each request (several conversations, where D-1010 has one); clearing the conversation when
    the tab closes (⌘W would lose a chat that *New Chat* exists to clear on purpose); keeping the Assistant in the stack
    as well (two places showing one widget).
- **D-1041 (2026-11-02, the Assistant knows the page beside its tab; the user's yes of 2026-11-02 to the follow-up that
  D-1040 left out; GUI, `agentprov assist`, tests and docs; class 0).** With the Assistant a tab beside a page
  (D-1040), "this page" or "here" in a question had no meaning to the model.
  - **Decision: what goes.** The page's name only, from a closed list: Viewer, Runs, Logs, System, Licences, Package,
    Docs (`agentprov.cli.assist.PAGES`; the GUI's `ASSIST_PAGES`, tested equal). It is the page in the window's first
    tab when the message is sent, which follows the sidebar. Nothing the page shows goes (no corpus, job, log or
    selection), so S2 and "nothing from a corpus is sent" (D-1010) hold. The line under the message field says which
    page goes with the next message.
  - **Decision: how it goes.** An optional `"page"` member of `agentprov-assist-request/0.1`, beside `"format"` and
    `"messages"`. It is additive: a CLI older than D-1041 reads only those two and ignores it, so a newer app with the
    `agentprov` 0.1.1 from PyPI (D-1030) still works, without the page. In a terminal, `--page NAME` (argparse choices;
    it wins over the request's member); the job form has it as an advanced choice (D-654 parity). A `page` that is not
    a string is a usage error; a string this CLI does not know is left out with a notice, so a newer app's page cannot
    break an older CLI's answer.
  - **Decision: what it changes.** The system prompt gains one sentence after the instructions: the user asks from the
    Assistant tab beside that page, what the page shows (a fixed description per page), and that "this page", "here"
    and "this screen" mean it. The page's name is a third passage query at weight 0.3 (the latest question 1.0, the one
    before it 0.5), so the guide's section on that page ranks a little higher without crowding out the question.
    `--show-context` prints `page: NAME` first. The reply format is unchanged.
  - **Rejected:** writing the page into the user's message text (it changes what the user wrote, and the transcript
    would show it); a new request format version (nothing removed or changed meaning; a version bump would break the
    PyPI 0.1.1 CLI); sending what the page shows, such as the selected job or the corpus open (corpus and log text are
    untrusted and are never sent, D-1010); probing `assist --help` for `--page` before each message (an extra CLI start
    for what the additive member gives for free).
- **D-1050 (2026-11-05, the software version a stage records is not a declared version; an addendum to D-30 that aligns
  it with H.8.4(2); audit 2026-11-05 finding AU-BND-1; the user's yes of 2026-11-05 to the audit's recommendation;
  class 0).** Every stage definition records `engine: agentprov@<software version>`, and D-30's declared identity (the
  definition minus `fn_digest`, `engine_code_sha256`, `adapter_code_sha256` and the digests beside an integer version)
  kept it. A release bump therefore changed the declared identity of every stage, so any changed output of a corpus
  built before the bump compared as `changed_explained`: `recompute --dry-run` exited 0 and `verify --level rederive`
  reported `unverified` where H.8.4(2) requires `unexplained_change` and exit 1.
  - **Decision.** `corpus.derive.declared_identity` drops `engine` too, as it drops the code digests and
    `limits_sha256`. The declared versions stay the ones H.8.4(2) names (adapter, profile, rule ids, spec, format) and
    the options, mode and library versions D-30 kept. `recompute`, `verify --level rederive` (which runs the same
    `Derivation.compare`), the `fn_digest` pairing of expansions (P-2) and `derive`'s refusal of a present layer at
    another version (N.2.3(4)) share the function, so a layer that differs from this build only in its software version
    is carried by `derive` rather than refused. The reuse key (D-30) is unchanged: it compares `fn_digest`, which still
    covers `engine`. H.8.4(2), the as-built note on H.8.4 and D-30's comparison bullet name `engine`.
  - **Why.** H.8.4(2) says a changed output with unchanged declared versions is unexplained "even if the code digest
    changed". The software version moves with every release whatever a stage did, so it behaves like a code digest: an
    intended change of an output needs a visible version bump of the stage (D9, D-31), not of the package. Keeping it
    turned every release into a blanket explanation for every difference, hiding unintended changes behind a version
    string (what D-30 rejected for code digests).
  - **Rejected:** listing the software version in `version_drift()` (D-430), so a recompute across a release is a drift
    report and `--out` refuses (every corpus would drift on each release, and a dry run would still explain every
    difference); keeping `engine` and documenting that H.8.4(2) does not hold across a release (the bump discipline
    would then check nothing after the first release); a notice when only `engine` differs (the comparison classes
    already say what matters, and the recorded definitions show the versions).
- **D-1051 (2026-11-05, a corpus derived or recomputed from a sealed corpus is not sealable; audit 2026-11-05 finding
  AU-BND-2; the user's yes of 2026-11-05 to the audit's recommendation, option C; class 0).** `derive --out` and
  `recompute --out` build the new working `corpus.json` from the source manifest. Over a sealed source its snapshots are
  the sealed H.2.3 form, which records the origin and no `pin` or `verification`, and a re-map passes the same missing
  pin on. `package` refused every such corpus as `package.refused.unpinned` ("no pin was recorded at import", D-33),
  while N.2.4(6) and the user guide (chapters 2 and 10) promised that the result is packaged as a new version. No test
  sealed a corpus derived from a sealed one, so the route had never worked.
  - **Decision (option C).** A derived corpus stays a working corpus for comparison. `package` recognises one whose
    `derived_from.state` is `sealed`, or that has any `derived_from` record and a snapshot in the sealed H.2.3 form (no
    `pin` member at all: a corpus derived from one derived from a sealed corpus records its immediate source's state,
    `working`, because `derived_from` records only the immediate source, but derive and recompute carry the sealed
    snapshots over unchanged; final review AU-FR-3; an import always writes the member, `null` when nothing was pinned,
    so a recompute of a working import that was never pinned keeps the accurate `unpinned` refusal, AU-NC-4), and
    refuses it first, before the other preconditions, with exit 4 and its own code
    `package.refused.derived`, saying that new corpus versions are made by re-importing the source and that a sealed
    corpus is reproduced by recomputing at its building commit (F-8). Every other corpus without a pin is still refused
    as `package.refused.unpinned`; a corpus derived from a working import keeps that import's pins and seals as before.
    N.2.4(6), the N.2.11 preconditions, the N.2.4 as-built note, H.1.5(3) and guide chapters 2, 5 and 10 say so.
  - **Why.** It matches practice: every new corpus version so far came from a re-import (D-31, D-430), and a recompute
    at this package of an older corpus is a drift report, not a new version. The promised route never worked, so
    nothing that was sealed depends on it. Sealing stays as strict as D-33 made it: a sealed origin is built from a pin
    the import observed. And a pin that no import observed cannot be recorded (invariant 2).
  - **Rejected:** (A) `package` accepting a sealed origin without a pin, trusting the source's seal (it loosens D-33 at
    the seal and needs a merge rule for the source's `WITHHELD.json`; left for a later decision if a re-release without
    a re-import is ever needed); (B) rebuilding a pin from the sealed origin (it records a pin and a verification that
    the import never observed, against invariant 2); leaving the `unpinned` refusal and only correcting the documents
    (the refusal would still name the wrong cause).
- **D-1060 (2026-11-05, one visual and form style for the whole GUI, with a terminal-command card wherever the CLI can
  do the action; the user accepted the mockup on 2026-11-05; GUI, tests and docs; class 0).** Each input screen had
  grown its own layout: Run Live was a long scroll of group boxes, form rows labelled with CLI flags, "More Options"
  under everything and the estimate at the bottom, and the other forms differed again. The user reviewed a mockup of
  Run Live, New Job, Settings, Package, a live run in progress and a style guide, and accepted it on 2026-11-05 for the
  whole app, the Viewer included.
  - **Decision: the nine rules.** (1) Grouped sections: related rows in a rounded card under a small capitalised
    heading, four or five sections a screen at most. (2) Plain labels, captions for detail: the label says what the
    field is in everyday words, a grey caption under it carries the one fact people need, and CLI flags and file names
    move to the tooltip (every earlier tooltip's information is kept). (3) Show only what applies: rows of a choice not
    made are hidden, not greyed (no Endpoint row while Scripted is chosen), and no row is left empty. (4) One Advanced
    level: rarely changed options sit behind one disclosure that says what it holds ("Advanced: …"), collapsed by
    default and remembered per screen; never a second level. (5) Defaults as placeholders: an unset number shows
    "Default (1,800)" in grey instead of the word "default" or a dash; the earlier special values map onto it, so the
    arguments a form builds do not change. (6) The right control: a segmented control for two to four exclusive
    choices, a switch for on/off, chips or a two-column checklist for many toggles, a short right-aligned field with
    its unit for numbers, a field with Choose… for paths (the long middle elided). (7) No horizontal scrolling: help text
    wraps, the form column is at most 680 px wide and scrolls only vertically. (8) Results stay visible: what the
    choices add up to (cells, cost, the command) sits in a summary panel or a card, not at the bottom of a long scroll.
    (9) Actions where macOS puts them: Cancel and the default button bottom right, the default blue; secondary actions
    bottom left.
  - **Decision: one theme, one set of components.** `gui/src/agentprov_gui/ui/theme.py` holds the light and dark
    palette tokens (from the Appearance setting; rebuilt when the colour scheme changes), the type scale (13 px body,
    11 px captions and section headings, 20 px page titles, the system font, scaled from the application font so View ›
    Bigger and Smaller still work) and the 8 px grid, and builds the one app-wide style sheet, applied once at startup.
    `ui/forms.py` holds the components every screen is built from: FormPage, FormSection, FormRow, Disclosure,
    SegmentedControl, Switch, ChipGroup, Checklist, IntField and DecimalField, PathField, StatusBadge, CommandCard and
    SummaryPanel. All text stays plain (S1): every text-bearing part is a `safe.py` label or a button's plain text,
    tooltips go through `safe.py`'s helpers, and every part has an accessible name. The reverse-parity walk (D-700)
    counts a composite input once, not its segments or chips.
  - **Decision: the terminal command card.** Wherever the CLI can do what a screen does, the screen shows the exact
    command in a monospace card with Copy, updated as the fields change, built by the same function that builds the
    job's argv (never a second copy of the logic). Keys never appear: a live run reads its key from the keychain
    (`--keychain`, D-702), and the job manager refuses `--env-stdin` and `--env-file` from the GUI. Copy copies one
    line per command; the card wraps with continuation backslashes, so it never scrolls sideways.
  - **Decision: Run Live first (phase A).** Run Live is rebuilt in this style: Benchmark, Model (Transport as a
    segmented control; the script for scripted runs; endpoint, model, price, key and containment for a real model),
    Limits (the D-725 caps, with "Use the quote's upper figure"), What to run (the full benchmark, the same arguments as
    ticking every suite and every attack that can be chosen, or suites as a checklist and attacks as chips; task
    selection and repeats behind one disclosure) and Save to (concurrency, attempts, canary, timeout, conformance, Tune…
    and every other `run` option behind "Advanced: …"). The summary panel shows the cells, cost, model calls,
    concurrency and the before-you-start checks; for a real model it is the quote for the run from `agentprov
    estimate` (its `quote` object read defensively, the estimate's own fields otherwise), always marked an estimate
    only, with how it is worked out (a fallback to the all-model figures is never called model-specific) and the upper
    figure labelled as what it is (the sum of per-cell 90th percentiles), and "Build cost figures from my corpora…"
    starts `agentprov priors build` as a confirmed job (D-1062). The card shows the `agentprov estimate` of the quote and
    the `agentprov run` that Start hands Runs. Every gate, the R1 and R2
    confirmations, the consent text, the caps, the estimate sequencing and the audit fixes (AU-GUI-3, AU-GUI-6, UC-9)
    are unchanged. The other screens follow in later phases.
  - **Decision: the Viewer in three panes (the user's yes of 2026-11-05 to the mockup).** The Corpora page is a split
    view after the macOS source-list pattern: on the left the corpora grouped by state (Sealed, Working, Being written,
    Unreadable) with their execution counts, a filter box and Open Folder…, the old corpora table's facts in a Corpus
    Details popover; in the middle the corpus header (name, state and verification badges, "N of M executions",
    Verify… / Revalidate…), the filters as applied-filter chips with + Add filter (each facet's values with counts)
    and Clear all, the executions table and a collapsed terminal-command line; on the right an inspector for the
    selected execution (badges, a segmented Graph · AER · SEM · PROV-JSON · Register · Validation · Raw · Index Row,
    Export Graph…, its command, Open in New Tab). Both side panes collapse to a labelled 34 px strip that names what
    it holds and reopens on a click, a toggle at the Viewer's tab bar, or View › Show/Hide Corpora (⌥⌘1) and
    Show/Hide Inspector (⌥⌘I; ⌥⌘0 is already Text Size › Default); widths and states are remembered and a narrow
    window collapses the inspector first. The filters are the same TableFilter and the same `agentprov stats
    --select` argv as the old pickers (tested per facet and value). Rejected: stacked collapsible sections (every
    collapse costs height and clicks, and the table and the details compete for it).
  - **Rejected:** a wizard for Run Live (the estimate and the gates depend on nearly every field, and staged disclosure
    fails for steps that depend on each other, as NN/g's guidance on progressive disclosure warns; a wizard would hide
    the cost while its causes are being chosen); keeping the per-screen layouts and fixing them one by one (the same
    problems, flags as labels, dashes for defaults, side scrolling, results at the bottom, would come back screen by
    screen); a second visual style for the Viewer (the user asked for the whole app to be consistent); a native
    platform form layout per OS (QFormLayout's AutoText labels are banned by S1, and the platforms' layouts differ in
    exactly the places the rules fix); showing a command assembled separately for the card (it would drift from what
    Start runs).
- **D-1061 (2026-11-05, Cancel Run: stop a job and mark it cancelled so that it is never resumed; the GUI redesign's
  running live run; `agentprov jobs`, the Runs page, tests and docs; class 0).** Runs had Pause (a drain), Resume, Stop
  and Force Kill, but no way to say "this run is finished with": a stopped run stayed one Resume away from spending more
  calls, from the app or from `agentprov jobs resume ID`.
  - **Decision: the command.** `agentprov jobs cancel ID` writes the mark `abandoned.json`
    (`agentprov-job-abandoned/0.1`: the job id, its state when cancelled and the UTC time) in the job's directory, then,
    while the job runs, sends the same graceful stop as `jobs stop` (the control file's `stop`, else one SIGTERM; exit
    130). A job that was already sent its SIGTERM by `jobs stop` (`stop.json` in its directory records that stop) is
    only marked too: the CLI takes a second SIGTERM as the hard abort (`os._exit(130)`), which would cut short the
    teardown the first one started (AU-NC-101). A job that has ended is only marked. A second cancel keeps the first mark. When the stop cannot be sent (the
    process identity no longer matches, or Windows without a control file) the mark stays and the command fails with
    `jobs.control.refused` (exit 4), naming `jobs kill ID --yes`. Nothing is deleted: the working corpus, the job's files
    and its lock rules are untouched.
  - **Decision: what the mark does.** `jobs resume` refuses a cancelled job with `jobs.resume.cancelled` (exit 4, a
    refusal); running the command again means starting it as a new job. `jobs list` and `jobs show` give
    `"abandoned": true` in JSON and `cancelled` in text. A mark that cannot be read still counts, so a damaged file
    never makes a cancelled job resumable. `jobs stop` is unchanged: a stopped job resumes as before.
  - **Decision: why a file of its own.** The supervisor rewrites `job.json` from its own copy while the job runs, so a
    mark written into `job.json` would be lost when the job ends.
  - **Decision: the Runs page.** The selected job's header shows its state as words with a tint (Running, Pausing,
    Paused, Stopping, Stopped, Cancelled, Ended, Failed), from its files: the control request, the cancel mark, the exit
    code and the progress file's `drained` outcome. **Cancel Run…** (Cancel Job… for other commands) asks first in the
    existing confirmation style and runs `jobs cancel ID` off the UI thread; Resume is disabled for a cancelled job and
    refused if reached. A live run's header also shows the billed model calls and the spend's upper bound against their
    caps, read from the working corpus's `live.caps` (in the pool, at most every 5 s); a run without caps shows neither.
    A command card lists `jobs drain`, `stop`, `resume`, `cancel` and `follow` with the job's real id, built from the
    same job forms as the actions.
  - **Not done: deleting the partial corpus.** No `agentprov` command deletes a working corpus (`purge` removes one
    leaked object and leaves a tombstone), so the app offers no "Delete partial corpus…" action; a user removes the
    folder by hand. A delete command would need its own decision (only a working corpus the run created, never a sealed
    one, confirmed with the path).
  - **Rejected:** a field in `job.json` (lost to the supervisor's rewrite, above); deleting the job directory as the
    cancel (the log, stderr and progress are the record of what the run did); a `--yes` on cancel (it deletes nothing,
    and a stop needs none); letting `jobs resume --force` override the mark (start the command as a new job instead).
- **D-1062 (2026-11-05, Run Live's cost quote: local priors from the user's sealed corpora, a `quote` object marked an
  estimate only, and a daily OpenRouter price refresh; amends D-650's "never automatic" and D-653's priors order; the
  user's request of 2026-11-05; CLI, settings, tests and docs; class 0).** Run Live must quote, in USD, what a run
  will cost for any model the user picks (a Claude model, DeepSeek, an OpenRouter model), from the traces of the
  corpora the user already holds where it can, and say plainly that the figure is an estimate.
  - **Decision: local priors.** `agentprov priors build [--corpus DIR]... [--jobs N] [--min-executions N]` counts the
    executions of the user's **sealed** corpora (every one under `$AGENTPROV_HOME/corpora`, the highest
    `corpus_version` of each corpus id; or the `--corpus` ones, each sealed, no corpus id twice) into
    `$AGENTPROV_HOME/estimate/priors-local.json`, written atomically, in the shipped priors' format
    (`agentprov-estimate-priors/0.1`). The row builder and the document writer moved from
    `tools/estimate/gen_estimate_priors.py` into `agentprov.estimate.localpriors` unchanged, and the tool now calls
    them, so both tables come from one implementation (a test rebuilds the old code path's bytes from the same inputs;
    the committed table re-serialises to its own bytes). The corpus reading is `agentprov.cli.priors_read`, because
    `estimate` sits below `corpus` in the import layers (M.5.2(1)). Corpora are read only through `CorpusReader`
    (the index streamed, each AER verified against its row, in worker processes for `--jobs`, at most four tasks per
    worker in flight); a working `.partial` tree, a `.withheld` sidecar, an execution `WITHHELD.json` names and an execution
    already counted in an earlier corpus (the same `ex`) are left out; nothing is written into a corpus. An `ex` counts
    as already counted only once its AER was read, so an unreadable copy never hides a readable one in a later corpus,
    and the executions counted do not depend on the corpora's order (AU-NC-103). A discovered corpus that cannot be read
    as a whole (a damaged index or `WITHHELD.json`, or no longer sealed) adds nothing and is named in
    `built_from.skipped` (`unreadable (<code>)`), as any directory `discover` cannot use; a `--corpus` one refuses the
    build naming its `--corpus` number, as one that is not sealed does (AU-NC-102). Only counts
    leave a worker; an execution whose benchmark, suite, attack or backend is not a plain label is left out
    (`unlabelled`), the model id becomes a family label as before. `built_from` names each corpus (id, version,
    manifest sha256, executions indexed, read, withheld, duplicate, unreadable) and each directory skipped, with no time
    and no worker count, so the same corpora give the same bytes at any `--jobs`. `agentprov priors show` (R0)
    describes the local and shipped tables.
  - **Decision: the order.** Per cell, `--stats-corpus` first, then per benchmark (the backend's, then the other
    AgentDojo-family one): local rows of this model family, shipped rows of this family, local any-model rows, shipped
    any-model rows; then `estimate.default.*`. The model family weighs more than whose corpora measured the row (a
    model's verbosity and call count drive its cost), and the user's own rows win where both tables have the same kind.
    Without a local file the order is D-653's, unchanged.
  - **Decision: the quote.** `agentprov estimate --format json` gains `quote` (additive; every other key keeps its
    meaning): `usd_p50`, `usd_p90` (plain decimal strings, as `cost_*`), `calls_*`, `tokens_in_*`, `tokens_out_*`
    (the run's totals, the preflight probe and judge calls included), `seconds_*` (at the run's `--jobs`, which the
    estimate models as `ceil(units / jobs)` rounds) and `seconds_serial_*` (the cells one after another), `jobs`,
    `cells` (the cell runs still due), `p50_aggregation` "sum of per-cell medians", `p90_aggregation` "upper (sum of
    per-cell 90th percentiles)", and `basis`: `priors` (`local`, `shipped`, `mixed`, or `null` when no cell used
    priors), `family_specific`, `family`, `executions` (behind the distinct rows used), `corpora` (the local priors'
    corpus ids, when used), `token_basis` (`chars/4`, `usage`, `mixed` or `null`), `price_source` (`direct`,
    `openrouter`, `override` or `local`), `price_as_of`, `discounts_assumed` (true only when measured cache reads are
    priced at a lower cache rate; batch prices are never used) and `estimate_only: true`. The text form adds "Estimate
    only: actual cost can differ (token counts are approximated as characters / 4; batch and cache discounts are not
    assumed).", worded from the basis when the tokens were recorded or a cache rate applies.
  - **Decision: p90.** The p90 cost stays what it was (D-650): per cell, the 90th-percentile calls times the cost of a
    call at the 90th-percentile tokens, summed over the cells. It is deliberately high (a run's total varies far less
    than one cell, and calls and tokens do not peak together) but it is not a quantile of the run's total, and a sum of
    quantiles is not a bound in general; so it is labelled "upper (sum of per-cell 90th percentiles)", never "p90 of the
    run". No other statistic is introduced.
  - **Decision: the daily price refresh.** The desktop app runs `agentprov prices refresh --allow-network --if-stale`
    as a CLI job the first time Run Live opens each day (the app keeps no network code, S11). The setting
    `prices.auto_refresh` (Settings: "Refresh prices once a day when Run Live opens"; unset means on, the user's choice
    of 2026-11-05) is the standing confirmation the job's R2 tier otherwise asks for, as `models.auto_refresh` is for
    model lists (D-733); the CLI checks it too, so a job started after the user turned it off fetches nothing.
    `--if-stale` fetches only when no snapshot was written today in this machine's local time (the user's day, not
    UTC's). A snapshot now records `written_at` (UTC) and `via` (`network` or `file`); `agentprov prices status
    --format json` (R0, no network) reports the newest snapshot's file, date, row count and `written_at` (from the
    file's time for a snapshot written before D-1062, which `written_at_from` says), the setting, `refresh_due` and
    `refresh_would_fetch`; the app shows the time in New Zealand time. A failed refresh leaves the newest snapshot in
    use, is shown, and never blocks Run Live. Direct provider prices (Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek publish no price API)
    stay the shipped table's rows with their date, and overrides still win.
  - **Rejected:** `agentprov estimate priors build` (the estimate's positional SOURCE leaves no room for a subcommand
    without rewriting argv); building local priors from working corpora (unsealed trees change, and withholding is
    decided at sealing); letting the local table replace the shipped one wholesale (a user with a few corpora would
    lose the shipped rows for every suite and family they lack); local any-model rows before shipped family rows (a
    model's own behaviour decides its cost more than whose runs measured it); a new statistic for the run's p90, such as
    a normal approximation over cells (the cells' joint distribution is not recorded, and an invented quantile would be
    presented as measured); a refresh on a timer or at app start (Run Live is where a price is needed, and a refresh
    nobody waits for is a network call without a reason); keeping the "once a day" test in the GUI (one
    implementation, the CLI's, D-700).
  - **Downstream effects.** No AER, SEM, PROV, corpus or manifest bytes change, and no stage digest moves (estimate/,
    cli/, jobs/tiers.py and settings.py are outside every stage scope). The shipped `estimate_priors.json` is unchanged.
    The GUI's forward parity (D-654) needs forms or exclusions for `priors build` (`--corpus`, `--jobs`,
    `--min-executions`, `--format`), `priors show`, `prices status` and `prices refresh --if-stale`.
  - **Tests:** `tests/estimate/test_local_priors.py` (old and new builder bytes, two sealed corpora with a withheld
    execution, a working corpus and an older version, determinism at `--jobs` 1 and 2, duplicates, the CLI, the order,
    the basis, the token totals, the quote),
    `tests/integration/test_estimate_cmd.py::test_the_quote_says_what_it_rests_on`, `tests/cli/test_prices_cmd.py` (status, the local day, `--if-stale` under the setting), `tests/jobs/test_jobs.py`
    (tiers), `tests/cli/test_cli_contract.py` (the command set).
- **D-1063 (2026-11-05, the 0.2.0 change batch: every recorded corpus-affecting finding is fixed; the user's yes of
  2026-11-05; regen-batch items 173–178; class 1).** The 2026-11-01 rule kept findings whose fix would change corpus
  results (stored AER/SEM/PROV bytes, counts, PROV statements, stage or adapter code digests) as records only. For
  release 0.2.0 the user decided to fix them all: the twelve such findings of the 2026-11-05 audit (AU-IMP-2 importer
  part, AU-IMP-3..6, AU-IMP-8, AU-IMP-9, AU-MSR-1, AU-MSR-2, AU-BND-3, AU-BND-4, AU-BND-6, AU-LIVE-4), the sixteen
  open ones of 2026-11-01 (UC-2, UC-12, UC-16..UC-22, UC-37..UC-43) and the excluded UC-44.
  - **Decision: scope.** The rule of 2026-11-01 is lifted for this batch only; later findings are again recorded first
    and batched by decision.
  - **Decision: sealed corpora.** No sealed corpus is rewritten. Each stays reproducible at its building commit (the
    F-8 ruling); a `recompute` at 0.2.0 of a corpus built before it is a drift report (H.8.4(5)).
  - **Decision: versions.** Catalogues, profiles and semantics tables whose bytes a stored corpus records are bumped
    and archived byte-exact (D-31); the stage and adapter code digests of every touched stage move for corpora built
    with 0.2.0. Each group's row (items 173–178) states its prediction: the digests that move, the families and the
    sealed corpora that would get different bytes or counts on re-import.
  - **Decision: capture/0.1 stays (the user's yes of 2026-11-05 to the recommendation).** UC-19/UC-20's writer and
    verifier changes (an early end, `error` then `session.end` or `session.end` alone at seq 1; the `value_adjusted`
    note kind) change no event type or data member, so the format id stays `capture/0.1`, amended in C.13 (writer items
    3 and 5, verifier item 15). An older verifier refuses an early-end log; logs say which writer made them
    (`session.start.writer.version`, `agentprov-capture` 0.2.0 from the release), and no published corpus holds capture
    logs. Rejected: `capture/0.2` (a version-axis change across code, schemas and spec for a more permissive grammar).
  - **Decision: the datasheet's raw-evidence sentence (AU-BND-3; the user's yes of 2026-11-05).** The `raw_included`
    claim keeps its predicate and its sentence now reads "The raw evidence of every snapshot is included in the corpus,
    except any item withheld from this release, which the Withheld items line counts and WITHHELD.json lists." It is
    true with or without withholding. Rejected: tightening the predicate, which would fail the next seal of the 45
    corpora that withhold raw objects until their cards cite another claim.
  - **Decision: the batch extended (the user's yes of 2026-11-05 to every recommendation).** The later reviews of
    2026-11-05 confirmed 21 more corpus-affecting findings, mostly incomplete earlier fixes: AU-RP-1, AU-RP-4..6,
    AU-NC-1, AU-NC-2, AU-NC-201, AU-NC-202, AU-NC-302..308 and AU-RC-1..6. They are fixed in the same batch (regen-batch
    items 181–184) under the same rules. AU-RC-4 (mcphunt-w2b, what-surrounds-w2: the `after` edges and their afterCausal
    statements move from the core to the inference bundle on re-import) and AU-RC-3 (dtap-bench-w2c: one execution's two
    "absent" annotations) are listed among the release notes' known issues of the sealed corpora. AU-RP-2 is settled
